title: kdash agents
description: Payload of kdash:agents — latest-value TS-OWNED (STRING JSON, no TTL), exactly 2 segments, on central (KDASH_CENTRAL_REDIS). The last `window_s` seconds (24 hours) of agent sessions across the fleet as BARS, for kpidash's Agents card (row 3, four cells): host-coloured bars, legs hung under their overseer, ship marks, and yellow for a session waiting on Ken. Contract v1 (CD-31). A bar is a STRETCH of activity, not a whole session: the publisher merges gaps it judges short and splits at longer ones, so one session may appear as several bars and `id` names a bar, not a session. Freshness is ts-first: judge `ts` against the record's own `expected_refresh_s` (kdash_cadence_stale). A still-running bar (`working` or `waiting`) carries the publish time as its `end`; the card draws the now line from its OWN clock, clips every `end` to now, and runs a running bar to now while the record is fresh — once it is stale, a running bar stops at its `end` (kdash_agents_bar_end). Field names are pinned; a rename, retype or removal lands as kdash:agents:v2 (rules.md Versioning), never in place.

ts.description: Unix seconds (float) when the publisher built the record, writer's clock. Bounded at 1e11 so a millisecond stamp fails instead of reading as permanently fresh.

expected_refresh_s.description: How long the publisher expects between its own scheduled writes, in seconds; 60 for ksitrep. Past this plus the reader's grace the record is stale: the card mutes, and running bars stop growing.

window_s.description: How far back the record looks, in seconds before `ts`; 86400 for the card. Every bar that ENDED within [ts - window_s, ts] is listed, so a host or hour with no bar inside the window is affirmatively idle, not unknown.

bars.description: Every activity stretch overlapping the window, sorted by `start` ascending. A bar that began before the window keeps its true `start`; the card clips it to the window's left edge. Empty when no agent ran in the window. Producer obligations the validator cannot check (no cross-field comparison, CD-24): `start` <= `end`; `end` >= ts - window_s; `end` <= ts; every `id` unique in the record; a `parent` names a bar in this record whose `overseer` is true, and not the bar itself. The C reader skips and counts a bar that breaks the first, second or fourth; it does not police the third, because the card clips `end` to its own clock anyway. A `parent` that breaks the last is dropped: the bar is kept, the link cleared and counted.

id.description: Opaque bar id chosen by the publisher, unique in the record, the host-token charset. Stable across writes for the same stretch where the publisher can manage it, but a reader never relies on that: it is only the target of `parent`.

host.description: Fleet host the session ran on (`kai`, `kubs0`, `cleo`), lowercase as `hostname` gives it. The card colours by it and falls back to its 'other' colour for a host it has no colour for.

name.description: What the card labels the bar with: the project the session works in, or the session's title. At most 31 CHARACTERS (UTF-8; the C reader counts characters, not bytes); the publisher truncates, the reader never does.

start.description: Unix seconds when the stretch began. May predate ts - window_s.

end.description: Unix seconds when the stretch ended; for a `working` or `waiting` bar, the publish time (`ts`). Never after `ts` and never before `start`.

state.description: `done`: the stretch is over. `working`: running now. `waiting`: still open and owes Ken an okay or a decision (ksitrep's `okay` and `decide` both map here); the card draws it yellow. A session that is only idle has no running bar: its last stretch is `done`.

shipped.description: A ship (a merged sprint) happened at `end`; the card draws a ship mark there.

overseer.description: This bar belongs to a session overseeing a program; legs hang beneath it and its name is drawn in the overseer colour.

parent.description: Optional: the `id` of the overseer bar this bar's session is a leg of. Absent when the bar is not a leg, or the overseer's bar is not in the record; never null, never empty.

x-counterexamples.why: `state` is one of done, working, waiting; an idle session's last stretch is `done`
`shipped` is required on every bar; no ship is `false`
`overseer` is a boolean, not a word
an absent link is ABSENT, not an empty string
an absent link is ABSENT, not null
`host` is a host token: no spaces
`name` is at most 31 characters; the publisher truncates
a millisecond `start` would sit far in the future
a window under an hour cannot fill the card
`window_s` absent: a record that does not say how far back it looks cannot say a host was idle
`expected_refresh_s` absent: the writer must declare its cadence (CD-28)
